title: Annotatio VI §.VI biblical: 1 Cor 11 guilty→eat Oral — reply via apostate guilt (Heb 6/10)
pass_a_gloss: The BIBLICAL, founding itself on the Apostolic saying 1 Cor. 11:28–29, so infers: Whoever of the Communicants become guilty of Christ’s body, those eat Christ’s body — if not spiritually, at least orally — the Impious &c. Therefore. Reply: How insipid the Major is, almost every abuse of Sacred things shows — by which men become guilty of GOD, of Christ, and of his body and blood, though not approaching the Eucharist. By the Holy Spirit Himself even Apostates are held guilty of Christ’s body and blood, though they have abominated all Christianity, much less the Sacraments: For they are said to crucify Christ and expose the Son of GOD to shame (Heb 6:4–6) and (ch. 10) to trample the Son of GOD and count the blood of the covenant common and insult the Holy Spirit. If therefore Apostates become guilty of Christ’s body and blood by deserting the sacrament, how will not Impious Christians become guilty of the same by abusing the Sacrament — i.e. by eating the Sacrament of Christ’s body and blood, not the Thing of the Sacrament, of which they deprive themselves even by abusing the Sacrament.
pass_b_english: Biblical press (1 Cor 11:28–29): whoever becomes guilty of the body eats it — if not spiritually, then at least orally — so the Impious eat. Therefore.

Reply: the major is thin — men become guilty of God and of Christ’s body and blood by many abuses without approaching the Eucharist. Apostates are guilty while deserting the sacrament (Heb 6; 10); Impious Christians can be guilty by abusing the sacrament (eating the sign, not the Thing).
source_text: BIBLICUM, in dicto Apostolico 1. Cor. 11. vers. 28. 29. se fundans, ita infert: Quicunque Communicantium, rei fiunt corporis Christi, illi manducant corpus Christi, si non spiritualiter, saltem oraliter, Impii &c. Ergo. Resp. Quam insulsa sit Major, rerum Sacrarum abusus fere quicunque ostendit, quô DEI, Christi, hujusque corporis & sanguinis, rei fiunt homines, Eucharistiam licet haud accedentes. Ab ipso Spiritu S. corporis & sanguinis Christi rei habentur ipsi etiam Apostatae, totum tamen Christianismum, nedum Sacramenta, abominati: Perhibentur enim crucifigere Christum & filium DEI ad ignominiam exponere Hebr. 6, 4. 5. 6. & Cap. 10. filium DEI conculcare & sanguinem fœderis profanum ducere, & Spiritum S. contumelia afficere. Quodsi ergo Apostatae rei fiunt corporis & sanguinis Christi, sacramentum deserendo, qui non rei fieri poterunt eorundem, Impii Christiani, Sacramento abutendo, i. e. manducando Sacramentum corporis & sanguinis Christi, non rem Sacramenti, quâ se privant ipsos, etiam Sacramenti abusu.

lemmas.gloss: not the Thing of the Sacrament
